patterns_found.visual_evidence: Both sketches show a compact input-like box in the top navigation/header area on the right side, consistent with a site search field; the reference HTML also includes a search form in that location.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Should accept text input and trigger a search on submit. On desktop this likely includes an explicit submit control; on mobile the smaller header treatment may rely on Enter/search-key submission or a compact submit affordance.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketches do not show whether results appear on a separate page versus live suggestions/autocomplete, so only submit/search behavior is clearly implied.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: The header search control is a form-like text entry element in both sketches, implying input handling and submission constraints.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Should validate basic search submission state, such as handling empty input gracefully and preserving focus/feedback if submission is invalid or no query is entered.
patterns_found.ambiguities: No explicit error state is drawn, so validation may be minimal and could be handled silently or by allowing empty submissions.

sketch_notes: These sketches imply a largely static informational page with very low JavaScript complexity. The only consistently evident interactive behavior across mobile and desktop is the header search form. No hamburger icon, dropdown trigger, tabs, accordions, modal triggers, sticky treatment, load-more affordance, or infinite-scroll cues are visibly indicated in the sketches. Cross-viewport differences appear mostly responsive/layout-based rather than behaviorally distinct, with the mobile header simply presenting a more compact search control.
